title: AI assistant to MCP: how the call is authorized
lede: Twenty numbered messages between eight participants: the connector is published, listed and added, then on first use the assistant is challenged, discovers the rules, authenticates the user through PingFederate and the enterprise IdP with PKCE, and the gateway swaps the token for a narrower on-behalf-of token before the private MCP server runs the tool. Simulated; every actor is an in-process mock. Product details are UNVERIFIED.

edges.label: Member adds it from the catalog
It appears in the member's agent
Route to the private MCP server

steps.title: Company publishes the connector
steps.what: Once, the company submits its connector (a manifest: name, publisher, MCP server URL, tool list) to the assistant's catalog. The manifest and the call are a MOCK; no real catalog's submission format is claimed (UNVERIFIED)

steps.title: Catalog reviews and lists it
steps.what: Organisational step, no protocol: the catalog reviews the submission and lists it. What a real catalog's review checks is UNVERIFIED (no standard or source is cited). The mock simply lists it; the status read shown is a stand-in

steps.title: Member adds it from the catalog
steps.what: The member picks the connector in the catalog and adds it, free, with nothing to install (a MOCK call; real catalogs differ and this is UNVERIFIED)

steps.title: It appears in the member's agent
steps.what: The connector shows up in the member's own agent, not signed in yet: state "added, not signed in". Sign-in and consent come on first use, which is when the next phase starts

steps.title: Asks a price question
steps.what: The user asks the assistant what an item costs

steps.title: Tool call with no token
steps.what: Calls the protected MCP tool with no token, gets 401 + WWW-Authenticate: resource_metadata (RFC 9728)

steps.title: Protected-resource metadata
steps.what: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource: authorization_servers lists PingFederate (RFC 9728)

steps.title: Authorization-server metadata
steps.what: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server: endpoints, S256, client identity (RFC 8414)

steps.title: Authorization request
steps.what: GET the authorization endpoint with code_challenge, method S256, resource and scopes (RFC 7636, RFC 8707)

steps.title: Front-channel redirect to the IdP
steps.what: PingFederate owns no user directory, so the browser is redirected to the enterprise IdP

steps.title: User authenticates
steps.what: The user authenticates at the enterprise IdP (password, passkey, MFA)

steps.title: Signed ID token
steps.what: Signed ID token (JWT) back to PingFederate, which then shows consent

steps.title: Authorization code + iss
steps.what: authorization_code, state and iss (RFC 9207) to the allow-listed redirect URI

steps.title: Code redemption
steps.what: POST the token endpoint with the code and the plaintext code_verifier (PKCE interlock)

steps.title: Access token
steps.what: access_token: aud = the public gateway, narrow scope, short TTL

steps.title: MCP request with bearer token
steps.what: MCP request with the access token; the gateway validates iss, aud, exp and scope

steps.title: RFC 8693 token exchange
steps.what: On-behalf-of token: act = the gateway identity, narrowed scopes, new audience (RFC 8693)

steps.title: Route to the private MCP server
steps.what: The private server re-validates the OBO token and enforces the per-API scope

steps.title: Result returns
steps.what: The structured result returns up the chain to the assistant

steps.title: Answer
steps.what: The assistant answers the user
